method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the three vertical graticule lines are meridians and all are bounded by the same top and bottom horizontal latitude lines. From the text, adjacent latitude differences are 5°, so the total latitude span between the top and bottom parallels is the same for all three meridians. Apply the rule that meridian arc length for a fixed latitude difference is identical on every meridian. Therefore the three meridian segments shown have equal length.

method.method_draft: Model the graticule from the image as spherical coordinates. Because the text says all graticule differences are 5°, the upper, middle, and lower parallels differ by 5° each, so the top-to-bottom latitude difference is 10° for the left, middle, and right meridians alike. For each meridian, compute length as R times the same angular latitude span, R·10° in radians.
